question: Can repeated training examples be reweighted using actual subgroup errors, without naming an encoder in the planner?
observation: A supervised primary trajectory already exists. For each measured weighted-fit-compatible linear pair encoder, compare its observed held errors on isolated pairs and on pairs from connected groups with repeated normalized text. We observed this discrepancy while generating the hypothesis, so only the two later group-disjoint folds can confirm it.
proposal: For both groups with at least 30 held examples, require a risk difference larger than the square root of the sum of binomial mean variances. Rank eligible real primary trials by measured accuracy, then gap significance and opaque configuration. At most two roots. Emphasize the higher-error stratum by a square-root power of connected fitting-group size, normalized to mean one; also test the opposite direction to check whether the hypothesis is misleading. Never look at a prediction batch to compute training weights.
selection: Compare each new classifier alone and equally averaged with the frozen measured two-model incumbent on the original primary training fold. For each selected root keep at most one strictly improving recipe. On confirmation_1 require a positive gain and at least 0.003 pooled gain across the two folds. Select the eligible recipe with highest worst-fold then pooled gain. Require another positive result on confirmation_2 before a separate cold anonymous integration. Do not alter the delivered default from this study.
resources: Up to four primary classifiers, two on confirmation_1 and one on confirmation_2; total at most seven new classifiers, including any failed attempt. Model API 0. External validation, course test and H2 are unavailable. The two existing reference classifiers are reused on each matched fold.
